accuracy.evidence: Hip height about 4 x footprint length is Alexander's (1976) working rule for dinosaur trackways; Henderson (2003) and Thulborn (1990) give 4 to 6 by group, which the adult text states. The walking and running thresholds (about 2 to 4 footprint lengths of space between prints for a walk, 6 or more for a run) follow from Alexander's relative stride limits (stride/hip height under 2 walking, over 2.9 running) with hip = 4 FL, so a pace gap of 3 FL is a walk and 7 to 8 FL a run. Print shapes follow Lockley (1991): theropod prints narrow with pointed claw tips, ornithopod prints broad with blunt rounded toes, sauropod prints large and round with a smaller crescent front print. Parallel trackways at Davenport Ranch (Bird 1944, Lockley 1991) are cited as a group. Parameterised answers 4*a, a and 30*a are whole numbers at every corner.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented slips in teaching trace fossils: wide gaps always mean running (gait predict, the giant trackway with a 180 cm gap but only 3 footprints, robot claim 2, m3, m8, challenge tag 'cm'), the hip is the size of the foot or far taller (size predict, per-option feedback, challenge tags 'foot' and 'ten'), every crowded track site is a herd (crossing trackways site, m6, challenge 'herd'), and prints reveal colour or sound (warm-up sorter, robot claim 3, m5, challenge 'colour').

lab_distinct.evidence: The lab reads evidence from tracks themselves: it draws theropod, ornithopod and sauropod prints from their real shapes, puts a print on a 10 cm grid and stacks four footprint lengths to the hip, fills the space between prints with ghost footprints to measure the gap in foot lengths, and draws whole track sites from above with parallel or crossing trackways. flagdino (real versus pretend dinosaurs) and flagfoss (how a fossil forms) do none of this, and the lab_distinct gate keeps flag_track.js under 30% similarity to every other lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner works each rule out by doing: the hip stack lights up four footprint blocks after a correct pick, the gait scene asks the child to tap the gap so footprints fill it before choosing, and the giant trackway's 180 cm gap holds only 3 footprints, so the child sees for themself why cm alone misleads. Wrong picks get the specific reason (thin pointed toes are claws; that is only the foot). Step summaries confirm each rule after the task.

predictions.evidence: The size predict sets 'About 30 cm' (the foot itself) against 'About 120 cm', and the grid scene then stacks four 30 cm footprints to the hip. The gait predict sets 'Yes, further apart means faster' against 'Not sure: count the gap in footprints', and the third trackway then shows a giant walking with wider gaps in cm than the small runner. The reveal names the child's own prediction.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating challenge questions, each with two tagged wrong answers. why() has eight messages: round (round prints are giants; pointed toes are claws), cannot (toe shape is a real clue), foot (that is only the foot, 4 x 40 = 160), ten (10 footprints too tall), cm (count the gap in footprints), herd (crossing trackways were made at different times), colour (tracks cannot show colour) and slow (8 footprints per gap means running). Each names the slip and gives the correct rule.

readability.evidence: Kid text uses short sentences and concrete words (toes, claw marks, mud, gap, footprints) and is within the validator's kid readability limit; the adult text names trace fossil, trackway, stride, theropod, ornithopod and sauropod and passes the adult limit. Lab banners shrink to fit and long tile labels such as 'Moving together' wrap onto two lines at 360 px.

no_filler.evidence: Each kid paragraph teaches one reading rule with numbers (toe shape, 4 footprints to the hip with the 30 cm to 120 cm example, 3 versus 6 footprints in a gap). The adult text gives the source of the size rule, two named mistakes with the fix, the Davenport Ranch example and what the lab does. The content gate finds no filler phrases and the explanation is under 12% similar to every other lesson.

mobile.evidence: Checked 390 px phone screenshots of every step in light and dark themes before and after Show me: the three toe-shape boxes sit in one row with two-line labels, the print card is about 130 px square, the grid and hip stack scale per dinosaur so the 5-square print and its 20-square stack both fit, trackway gaps are tappable boxes at least 60 px wide, and the robot buttons are 60 px tall. Every canvas action also has a full-width button under the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: the three toe shapes (named with the print number), the three hip heights (named with the footprint length), Fill the gap, Walking and Running, Moving together and Not together, and Right or Slip. The gap length is given in words and numbers as well as drawn, so the task does not depend on seeing the prints. The canvas aria-label is updated with every message, challenge feedback is a polite live region, and the walk gate's axe run is clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
